debate_outcome_batch2.agreement: Both models independently converged on the same 3 verdicts despite opposing stances:
decided: C9 coder model tier: SHIP NOW. Low-risk, cheap — a step-tag router (author vs. ops/bulk) with an ordered allowlist + fallback. Both models proposed concrete model ids, but both hallucinated ids outside sauron's real roster — SEE grounded_coder_tier below for the corrected, roster-verified list.

opencode/aider backend: SHIP LATER, explicitly gated behind A/B5/B7 landing first and proving the baseline LLM-writes-full-file flow. Minimal shape = thin subprocess wrapper + adapter behind a config flag (default off), NOT a full SDK integration. Reuse the same wrapper shape for aider later.

gated_claude: DROP ENTIRELY (unanimous, not just lower priority). Both models called it scope-creep that directly undermines the repo's own 'never Claude' cost invariant; the correct escape valve for a genuinely hard step is better prompt engineering / task decomposition in C9, or a documented manual-fallback procedure the USER runs themselves outside sauron — sauron itself must never offer or gate a Claude path.

second_batch_ship_now.name: whole-file replacement edit protocol
second_batch_ship_now.desc: Change the mission edit protocol so the writer emits full replacement file content (files[]) rather than byte-exact old->new snippet edits, for any file under ~B5's size threshold. Keep edits[] (surgical snippet form) only as an opt-in path for tiny single-line changes where the model explicitly chooses it. Validate every whole-file write via the B5 compile/lint gate before accepting it.
second_batch_ship_now.why: Debate-decided in batch 1: diffs/snippets demand hunk/context alignment that weak models silently botch; a whole file is trivially validated via ast.parse/compile.
second_batch_ship_now.wiring: providers/router/mission.py: _WRITER_SYS (prompt instructs files[] full-content form as default), _execute_plan (branch: files[] -> write+B5-validate; edits[] -> existing snippet path, now explicitly legacy/opt-in).
second_batch_ship_now.depends_on: B5 compile-gate (batch 1) must land first — this item's acceptance test asserts the compile gate is invoked on every files[] write.
second_batch_ship_now.test_first: New test monkeypatches dispatch.generate to return a files[] payload with intentionally broken syntax; assert _execute_plan calls the B5 validator (not just that B5 exists) and rejects/repairs before marking the step done.

second_batch_ship_now.name: cross-iteration no-progress / stall detector
second_batch_ship_now.desc: Track verify-gate verdicts and error signatures across mission iterations. If N (default 3, env PAL_MISSION_STALL_N) consecutive iterations show no forward progress — same failing verify command, identical error string/symbol, or no new files_written/edits_applied — escalate: either fall back to the deterministic/non-LLM path where one exists, or abort the mission with a clear 'no progress after N iterations' reason instead of silently burning the step budget.
second_batch_ship_now.why: qwen3 flagged this as the missing guard in batch 1's own debate; generalizes the per-step dedup in execution-guard (A2) to the iteration level — this is what would have cut short the observed 4-iteration failed refactor.
second_batch_ship_now.wiring: providers/router/mission.py: run_mission loop (track last-N verdicts/error-signatures in a small ring buffer) and run_panel (same check across panel rounds).
second_batch_ship_now.test_first: New test drives run_mission with a mocked writer that always returns the same failing output; assert the loop stops at iteration N+1 with an explicit stall reason, not at the flat max-steps limit, and does NOT report false COMPLETE.

second_batch_ship_now.name: symbols-called acceptance (grep form only)
second_batch_ship_now.desc: When a mission's plan claims to add a new function/class, the acceptance/verify step greps the rest of the touched files (and, cheaply, the immediate repo) for an actual call site of that symbol — not just that it's defined or importable. Stays a plain grep/regex check; explicitly do NOT build a call-graph or static-analysis pass (brittle on dynamic Python, batch 1 already ruled this out).
second_batch_ship_now.why: Cheapest possible guard against the exact 'dead code passed the gate' failure class (helper defined, never wired).
second_batch_ship_now.wiring: providers/router/mission.py: _deterministic_gate / _gate_verdict — add one more cheap check alongside existing verify-command execution.
second_batch_ship_now.test_first: New test: plan claims to add function foo(), writer emits foo() defined but never called anywhere in the diff/repo; assert the gate flags it (COMPLETE withheld) even though verify commands pass.
